newsitem.title: UK: Brent crude begins week a little lower.
newsitem.headline: Brent crude begins week a little lower.

text.p: North Sea Brent began the week's trading on the low side in a quiet physical market on Tuesday and also eased a little on the paper market, traders said.

A minimum Brent cargo loading May 17-19 was sold by a European major to a Wall Street trader for June Brent -28 cents. The trader sold a May 16-18 Brent on Monday for the same price, eight cents lower than a deal on Friday.
The major also repurchased a 600,000 barrel cargo of Norwegian sweet Oseberg from a Norwegian seller for Dated Brent +14 cents. The cargo is for May 17-19 loading.
Traders also said one cargo of Ekofisk loading May 25-27 changed hands on Monday or Friday but the price was not immediately available.
The buyer of the Norwegian crude had sold a May 25-27 Palanca to the seller and "seems like it (buyer) collected two or three cents on it", one European trader said.
On the cash market, IPE June Brent was five cents down at $17.92 a barrel by 1158 GMT.
Brent intermonth spreads were largely unchanged or slightly easier.

Jun/Jul traded once at June Brent -15 cents after changing hands at -14 cents in late U.S. trade. May/June was almost unchanged from Friday, talked -21/-14 cents while July/Aug was two to three cents weaker at -14/-12 cents.
July Brent partials were quoted at $18.10-$18.12 in late U.S. trade, down from Friday's $18.15-$18.18.
However, Brent CFDs firmed, with next week's offered five cents higher at about June -25 and May 19-23 gaining six cents at July -36/-33, or the equivalent of June Brent -20/-19 cents.
Two Brent cargoes were said to be turning wet on Tuesday, traders said.
